psf_cap_vs_market_gap.read: Since June the market has risen against the fixed $2.2M cap, tightening the intersection especially in D15. The June 'The Line @ $2,054 psf' match was a low outlier that has since cleared and re-rated to $2,560+ psf.

filter_tradeoff_insights: TENURE is the binding constraint on the big-development angle: every 200+ unit development with a size+price-fitting 3BR stack (Kovan Regency 393, Kovan Residences 521, Kovan Melody 778, Silversea, Sanctuary Green, Costa Rhu, Water Place, Florence/Riverfront) is 99-yr leasehold. The only large FREEHOLD developments (One Amber, The Esta, Sea View, Gazania) price >=1,000 sqft units at $2.7M+. You cannot get large-development liquidity + freehold + >=1,000 sqft + <=$2.2M at once - pick 3 of 4.

Every clean pass is a SMALL/BOUTIQUE project (Bliss 140, Quinn 139, Palm Grove 111, Residences Botanique 81, Carpmael 16, Paya Lebar 117) -> low liquidity and thin transaction data. The size condition + FH + budget structurally forces you into low-unit-count projects.

REGION: relaxing to D19 (and D14 Paya Lebar) is what makes family-size fit the budget. D15 freehold has re-rated above the cap (TEL fully priced in); D15 now forces either <1,000 sqft or >$2.2M. D19 is the value district for size.

PSF-vs-SIZE along the cap line: Carpmael 1,076 sqft@$2,045 vs Palm Grove 1,282 sqft@$1,638 vs Bliss 1,765 sqft@$1,246 - all $2.0-2.2M but psf halves as you buy space. Sweet spot: ~1,050-1,300 sqft 3BR in D19/D14 FH at $1,600-2,000 psf.

The 'not a new launch' filter is now actively rejecting fresh 999-yr D19 stock that passes on every other axis (Jansen House: $2.038M / 1,012 sqft / 999-yr / D19, fails only on being a new launch). As 2024-26 boutique launches TOP, decide whether to relax this for just-completed 999-yr resale.
